   526	\approx_{\sqrt{\eps_\omega}} -\Id \ot M^{\Variable_5,\omega} M^{\Variable_1,\omega}$,
   527	the anticommutation consequence for the second player, which is then
   528	averaged over $\omega$ with Jensen's inequality.  The corrected theorem needs
   529	in addition the agreement distances $\Delta_1(\strategy_\omega)$ and
   530	$\Delta_5(\strategy_\omega)$.
   531	They are available from the lemma, but three transports are needed besides the
   532	triangle inequality, and they are worth spelling out.
   533	\begin{enumerate}
   534	  \item \emph{Question distribution.}  Item~7 averages over \emph{anticommuting}
   535	  $\omega$: it states that the first player's trace-postprocessed point
   536	  measurement $\{P^{X,\omega}_a\}$, the $X$-basis point measurement at
   537	  $u_X$ postprocessed by $a \mapsto \tr(a\,r_X)$ --- where
   538	  $\omega = (u_X, u_Z, r_X, r_Z)$ --- agrees with the second
   539	  player's $\Variable_1$ measurement,
   540	  $P^{X,\omega}_a \ot \Id \simeq_\eps \Id \ot M^{\Variable_1,\omega}_a$.
   541	  Item~1, by contrast, averages over the \emph{full} question distribution of
   542	  the Pauli basis test and gives the self-consistency of the point
   543	  measurements only under that distribution.  Combining the two therefore
   544	  requires first conditioning item~1 on the anticommutation event and on the
   545	  point question type.  Both are events of probability bounded below by a
   546	  universal constant --- for the anticommutation event this is
   547	  \path{fact:omega-anticomm-prob} --- and the quantity being averaged is
   548	  nonnegative, so conditioning multiplies the bound by the reciprocal of that
   549	  probability and item~1 holds on average over anticommuting $\omega$ at the
   550	  cost of a constant factor.
   551	  \item \emph{Postprocessing and observables.}  Item~1 concerns the point
   552	  measurements $\{M^{(\mathsf{Point},W),u}_a\}$, whose outcomes are field
   553	  elements, whereas the defect \eqref{eq:defect} involves binary measurements:
   554	  the trace postprocessing on the point side and, on the Magic Square side, the
   555	  relabeling of the game's answers to a bit. For projective measurements on
   556	  opposite registers, the summed squared distance is twice the consistency
   557	  defect. Coarse-graining preserves projectivity and decreases that defect:
   558	  it removes nonnegative terms from the sum over disagreeing outcomes.
   559	  Thus it does not increase the distance in this application. This argument
   560	  does not assert distance monotonicity for arbitrary POVM effects.
   561	  The passage between effects and observables uses the binary normalization
   562	  identity, which is what the Lean form of
   563	  item~1 requires: \leanid{MIPStarRE.QPBT.pointObs\_self\_consistent} compares
   564	  the two players' $\pm1$-valued point observables under the uniform
   565	  distribution on the point $u$, while \eqref{eq:defect} is a sum over the two
   566	  effects.  For a two-outcome projective measurement the effects are
   567	  $(\Id \pm \mathcal O)/2$, so the summed squared effect distance is one half
   568	  of the squared observable distance, and the two forms differ by a factor
   569	  $2$.
   570	  \item \emph{Swapped state.}  The defect \eqref{eq:defect} compares
   571	  $A^{\Variable_j}_b \ot \Id$ with $\Id \ot B^{\Variable_j}_b$ on $\ket\psi$ in

   573	  orientation, and its Lean form states that reversed estimate on the swapped
   574	  state, the image of $\ket\psi$ under the exchange of the two tensor factors.
   575	  Transporting an estimate from the swapped state back to $\ket\psi$ is that
   576	  same exchange applied to the operators as well; it is an isometry, so the
   577	  estimate is preserved.
   578	\end{enumerate}

   100	\begin{remark}
   101	We note that the quantum low-degree test, as stated in \cite{NV18a}, does \emph{not} have value-$1$ real commuting EPR strategies.
   102	This is because it uses as a subroutine the standard magic square game,
   103	and the magic square game does not have value-$1$ real commuting EPR strategies.
   104	Its value-$1$ strategies \emph{are} EPR strategies,
   105	and they \emph{are} real (all observables are either $X$ or $Z$, with the sole exception of the $Y \otimes Y$ observable,
   106	which can be rewritten as $Y \otimes Y = -(X \otimes X) \cdot (Z \otimes Z)$, manifestly real).
   107	But they are not commuting, because each row and column have at least one pair of noncommuting observables.
   108	
   109	Consider instead the following ``oracularized" version of the magic square game:
   110	one player is given a random row or column (and is expected to play as in the normal magic square game),
   111	and the other player is given a random cell in that row or column,
   112	and the verifier simply checks that they agree on that cell.
   113	In addition, with some constant probability, both players are given the same cell and their answers are checked against each other.
   114	In this case, all observables measured are commuting, and so this variant has a value-$1$ real commuting EPR strategy.
   115	In addition, it certifies the same state and measurements as the normal magic square game,
   116	and so we can use it as a subroutine in the quantum low-degree test instead.
   117	\end{remark}

import MIPStarRE.QPBT
import Lean

open Lean Elab Command

elab \"#review_ms_dependencies\" : command => do
  let env ← getEnv
  let roots : Array Name := #[
    "'``MIPStarRE.QPBT.pointObs_twisted_commutation,
    ``MIPStarRE.QPBT.pointObs_twisted_commutation_interchanged,
    ``MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_combinedPointsWitness,
    ``MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_globalPairWitness,
    ``MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness,
    ``MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness_qubit,
    ``MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_spcc_value_one,
    ``MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ld_soundness]
  for root in roots do
    let mut todo : Array Name := #[root]
    let mut seen : NameSet := {}
    while !todo.isEmpty do
      let n := todo.back!
      todo := todo.pop
      if seen.contains n then continue
      seen := seen.insert n
      if let some ci := env.checked.get.find? n then
        todo := todo ++ ci.type.getUsedConstants
        match ci with
        | .thmInfo info => todo := todo ++ info.value.getUsedConstants
        | .defnInfo info => todo := todo ++ info.value.getUsedConstants
        | .opaqueInfo info => todo := todo ++ info.value.getUsedConstants

    if seen.contains ``MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_ms_rigidity then
